_README: THE PART OF THE CATALOGUE THAT CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM A FILE.
tools/gen_payload_catalog.py walks the owner's folder and reads out of the files themselves
everything a file can tell you: platform (from the folder), size, sha256, and for a package its
title, title id, content id and version straight out of param.sfo/param.json. What a file CANNOT
tell you is which port proves it is running, whether it is safe to start unattended, and which
GitHub project it came from. Guessing any of those has already cost this project real time:
ShadowMount was listed at port 9021 (which belongs to elfldr and is always bound), so the
'is it already up?' test was permanently true and it was never actually started for months.
So those three facts are written down here, by hand, once, with a reason each. An id that is not
in this file still appears in the panel - it just has no port, no upstream and a neutral state,
which is the honest answer rather than a green light nobody can back.
FIELDS
title      what the panel calls it. Absent - the folder name is used.
blurb      one plain sentence. Shown under the title.
port       the TCP port that PROVES it is running, and on the PS5 it doubles as the
auto-start rule in payload_bundle.h: >0 means 'start at boot if that port is free'.
Absent or 0 means there is nothing to observe - the tile says so instead of lying.
autostart  may the console start this by itself at boot? Only ever true for a payload that
provides a service and touches nothing underneath it.
layer      'jailbreak' marks a payload that changes the jailbreak layer. Those are never
auto-started and the panel warns before loading one. payload_bundle.h already
states the rule: that is the owner's call to make, never a side effect of ours.
repo       owner/name on GitHub, for the release check. SHOWN ON THE TILE, because several of
these names have more than one fork and pointing an updater at the wrong fork would
put someone else's build on the console. Visible is fixable; silent is not.
asset      substring that picks this file out of a release's asset list.
source_index   the page a project publishes its own builds on, when that is not GitHub.
source_match   the link prefix on that page that identifies a download, with the version
immediately after it - "/download/ps5/PKGI13337/" matches
"/download/ps5/PKGI13337/1.10.0". MAY BE A DICT KEYED BY PLATFORM, and
for Itemzflow it has to be: pkg-zone publishes its PS4 and PS5 builds behind
separate links, on different version numbers. (FPKGi's two links are ONE
file - same length, same bytes, the sha256 GitHub publishes.) One curated
entry serves both consoles, so the dict is collapsed to this item's own
platform in _curated_source().
BOTH OR NEITHER. Half of a direct source is worse than none: the lane would
skip GitHub and then have nothing to address, so half is discarded.
The console reads these itself - a browser cannot, because the fallback
that reads api.github.com from the console's own browser works only thanks
to GitHub's Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and these hosts send none.
There is no published checksum at the far end, so such a download is checked
against its own Content-Length, against the first bytes a package has to
begin with, and - when the catalogue already recorded that very version -
against the size and sha256 recorded here. A second source is tried when
the first does not answer: an entry that names both a page and a `repo`
falls back to the GitHub project, which for FPKGi is the same bytes.
ours       true for our own artifacts. They are listed but never embedded as a copy of
ourselves - that is the recursion ps4-app/build-all-wsl.sh exists to prevent.
WHAT IT IS AND WHERE IT GOES
catalog    true: this exists even when no folder holds it, so it is OFFERED (the Download
drawer) on a PC that has never had it. Needs `platform` or `platforms`.
platform   PS4 or PS5 - which console an offered entry is for.
platforms  ["PS4", "PS5"] when one entry serves both and is offered once for each.
title_id   the console's own id for the app. What 'Installed' is matched against, and what
the console checks an archive's app folder against before placing it.
ext        the file type the release asset must have. Default .pkg for a homebrew and .elf
for a payload; most emulators ship a .zip and must say so.
emulates   what an emulator plays. Shown on the tile.
fw / homepage / note   shown in the tooltip. `note` is the one sentence about setup.
source_only  true: listed, but the project publishes no build this app can fetch.
WHAT IT NEEDS BESIDE ITS OWN FILE - each of these is 'put a file in a folder', done for the owner
extras       [{asset, ext, why[, place]}] - other files from the SAME release that the app
does not work without (a helper ELF). Downloaded with it; a helper is put in
Payload Manager's folder when its app is installed and is NEVER started by us.
data_dirs    {"<folder in the archive>": "/data/..."} - a tree that travels beside the app
inside its archive and belongs somewhere else on the console. Nothing that is
already there is overwritten.
data_files   {"<NAME>": {dest, create, json_key, stock, stock_max}} - ONE NAMED FILE that
travels with a package. The key is the name looked for BESIDE THE PACKAGE in
the owner's folder (case ignored - Windows has none); `dest` is the exact path
on the console and its spelling is the contract. `create` is the smallest
valid document, written only when the console has no such file and the owner
has none either. `stock`/`stock_max` recognise the placeholder the homebrew
writes for itself on first launch - nobody's data - which the owner's file may
replace. `json_key` is the top-level key a valid file carries.
THE OWNER'S FILE IS NEVER PART OF THIS APP: it is read from their folder at
the moment it is sent and goes nowhere else - not into the catalogue, not into
a build, not into the repository.
console_lines  {"/data/<file>": ["<line>", ...]} - lines that must be present in a text
file on the console. Added when missing, LF endings only, nothing else in the
file is touched.
place        the exact console path a file is WRITTEN to, under that name, instead of being
run, installed or opened. On an entry it is the main file's; on an `extras`
item it is that file's, and `?` in the directory part stands for one character
of a folder that must ALREADY exist (it is matched, never created). A file
already at an extras place is replaced only on a second, deliberate press.
needs        what has to be running on the console for this to work at all, as a sentence.
A dict keyed by platform when it differs - shown on that console's tile only.
bundled      {"PS5": "seed/PS5/<file>"} - the file this app carries for an entry that has
no download address anywhere. Only for an entry with no `repo` asset and no
`source_index`: never embed what can be fetched.
CONTENT, NOT FILENAME (3.84.0). A file can be renamed - the owner said so plainly - so identity
must come from what is INSIDE it:
marker   a byte string that appears in this project's binary and in no other one here. The
catalogue matches on this first, so ftpsrv-ps5.elf renamed to anything at all is still
recognised as ftpsrv, with its port, its upstream and its warnings intact.
ver_re   a regex with one group that reads the version OUT of the binary. kstuff, Payload
Manager and the WebKit installer all carry theirs; the rest do not, and for those the
filename is the only source - which the catalogue records as version_from so the panel
never presents a guess as a fact.
probe    how to test `port`. Absent means a TCP connect. "udp" means the console tries to BIND
the port instead - the only test that works for a service which listens on UDP and
answers nobody, which is exactly what nanodns does.

ftpsrv.title: FTP server
ftpsrv.blurb: Serves the console's filesystem over FTP, which is how files are moved on and off it.

nanodns.title: nanodns
nanodns.blurb: A tiny DNS server, used to point the console away from Sony's update servers.
nanodns.note_port: Answers on UDP 53. A TCP connect proves nothing and a DNS query from the LAN gets no reply even when it IS running (measured on both consoles), so the console tests it by trying to BIND that port: if the bind is refused, something already holds it.

kstuff.title: kstuff
kstuff.blurb: Part of the jailbreak itself. Already running if your console is jailbroken.

shadowmountplus.title: ShadowMountPlus
shadowmountplus.blurb: Mounts game backups from a drive so the console can see them as installed games.
shadowmountplus.note_port: 10101, NOT 9021. It announces its own listener: http://127.0.0.1:10101/api/v1
shadowmountplus.note_marker: The banner, not the bare name: 'ShadowMount' is also in any program that only talks to its API, and one such ELF dropped in this folder would have been read as ShadowMountPlus.

pldmgr.title: Payload Manager
pldmgr.blurb: Loads other payloads, and the only thing that can start one for us. Leave it running.
pldmgr.note_autostart: Never auto-started: it is what starts things, and relaunching a live loader is how installs get wedged.

onionhen.title: OnionHEN
onionhen.blurb: A homebrew enabler. Changes the jailbreak layer, so it is yours to start, not ours.

webkit-autoloader-installer.title: WebKit autoloader installer
webkit-autoloader-installer.blurb: Installs the autoloader onto the home screen, so the console can re-jailbreak itself.

pkg-mutant-shop.title: PKG MUTANT SHOP
pkg-mutant-shop.blurb: This app. Listed so you can send it to a console that has just been jailbroken.

ps4mount.title: PS4Mount
ps4mount.blurb: Mounts PS4 game packages from a USB drive so the PS5 runs them without installing them.
ps4mount.fw: PS5 - its author tested 13.20; reported working on 13.60
ps4mount.note: one file, started once per boot; put the packages in the root of an exFAT USB drive - it moves them into ps4/<title id>/ on that drive; its own panel is at http://<PS5 IP>:8770 and in the Media tab
ps4mount.note_port: 8770/TCP on every interface is its web panel (src/web.h WEB_PORT). 9032 is a single-instance lock on loopback only and proves nothing from outside.
ps4mount.note_autostart: Never auto-started: on start it scans every USB and extended drive, MOVES each PS4 game package it finds in a drive root and registers it with the system. That is the owner's call.

y2jb-autoloader.title: Y2JB Autoloader
y2jb-autoloader.blurb: Jailbreaks the console from the YouTube app, then starts your payloads by itself.

extras.why: the first install - the YouTube app's whole data image (321 MB) with the autoloader inside it

y2jb-autoloader.note: not a payload file and not a package: it lives inside the YouTube app's own data, so the YouTube app has to be installed first. download0.dat is the install; y2jb_update.zip is the update, which the autoloader reads the next time YouTube is opened and then removes
y2jb-autoloader.note_port: Nothing to observe. It runs inside the YouTube app, which it closes once the console is jailbroken.
y2jb-autoloader.note_place: /data/y2jb_update.zip is one of the places the autoloader's own updater looks (src/update.js). /user/download/PPSA0165?/ is the author's own instruction, and the ? stands for the region of the YouTube app that is installed (PPSA01650, 51 or 52) - matched against a folder that already exists, never created.
y2jb-autoloader.note_updates: Its test builds are published in the same list as its releases; the newest release is what is offered.

ITEM00001.title: Itemzflow Game Manager
ITEM00001.blurb: A game launcher and manager that runs on the console itself.
ITEM00001.note: published on pkg-zone rather than on GitHub - the project's GitHub page carries the changelog and points there for the package - with a separate build per console, each on its own version number

LAPY20009.title: PS4-Xplorer
LAPY20009.blurb: A file browser for the PS4, with FTP and package installing built in.
LAPY20009.note: published on pkg-zone by its author; that page can be a version behind a copy obtained elsewhere, and a newer copy you already hold is never replaced by an older one

MOUU12023.title: Internet Browser
MOUU12023.blurb: Puts a browser on the home screen, so the console can reach a page without a PC.
MOUU12023.note: has no public download address, so this app cannot fetch it - a copy in your own Homebrews/PS5 folder is sent like any other
MOUU12023.note_format: Begins \x7fFIH, not a package header this app reads. Its name comes from the param.json inside it, and the console decides whether it installs.

PKGI13337.title: FPKGi
PKGI13337.blurb: Browses and installs packages from a list you host yourself.

needs.PS5: needs etaHEN on a PS5, with its Direct PKG Installer switched on

PKGI13337.note: one package for both consoles - the PS4 and PS5 links on pkg-zone are the same file, and the GitHub project publishes the same bytes with a checksum, so it is fetched from whichever answers. A GAMES.json kept beside the package in your folder is put on the console with it; an empty one is created when there is none
PKGI13337.note_asset: 'pkgi' because it has to match both names this file is published under: PS4_PKGI13337_v1.10.0.pkg on pkg-zone and FPKGi_v1.10.0-release.pkg on GitHub.
PKGI13337.note_needs: On a PS5 it asks etaHEN to let it out of its sandbox and installs through etaHEN's installer on 127.0.0.1:9090 (its own source, UnityOrbisBridge unity.cpp and pkg.cpp). A PS5 that runs neither opens it and nothing happens. A PS4 needs nothing extra.

PPSA99169.title: RetroArch (PS5)
PPSA99169.blurb: Many systems in one front-end - PS1, PSP, SNES, N64, Mega Drive, arcade and more. Each system is a separate core, published beside the app.
PPSA99169.emulates: PS1 · PSP · SNES · N64 · Sega · arcade · more
PPSA99169.note: one 752 MB archive; the cores are inside it, in cores/, with their data in info/
PPSA99169.note_shape: PPSA99169 is an extracted app folder (eboot.bin + sce_sys/param.json + assets), which is what ShadowMountPlus mounts. It is not a .pkg and must never be sent down the package lane.

dolphinps4.title: DolphinPS4
dolphinps4.blurb: GameCube and Wii games, running natively on the PS4.

ps5sx2.title: PS5SX2
ps5sx2.blurb: PlayStation 2 games on the PS5, derived from PCSX2.

extras.why: its helper payload - nothing starts without it

ps5sx2.note: its helper payload must be running before the emulator starts - a PC installing it puts the helper in Payload Manager too; installed from the console alone, add the helper yourself. PCSX2 settings and patches live in /data/PCSX2
ps5sx2.note_extras: 'ps5sx' because the helper has been published as PS5SXHelper.elf, ps5sx2-aio.elf and ps5sx2-bot.elf in eight days. The main archive is PS5SX2-<tag>.zip and is picked by `asset`+`ext`, so the two cannot be confused.

ps5x360.title: PS5X360
ps5x360.blurb: Xbox 360 games on the PS5. Developed and tested on 13.60.

extras.why: collects a log when a game will not start

ps5x360.note: games go in one folder each under assets/roms/ inside the app

xpsemu.title: XPSemu
xpsemu.blurb: Original Xbox games on the PS5, based on Xemu.

extras.why: has to be running for the emulator to start

xpsemu.note: the helper payload must be running before the emulator starts; your games and saves live in /data/xemu, outside the app

prosperoeden.title: ProsperoEden
prosperoeden.blurb: Nintendo Switch games on the PS5.
prosperoeden.note: your games and saves live in /data/prosperoeden, outside the app

ps5cemu-har.title: PS5CEMU-HAR
ps5cemu-har.blurb: Wii U (Cemu) and Nintendo 3DS (Azahar) on the PS5.

porpoise.title: Porpoise
porpoise.blurb: GameCube and Wii games on the PS5, Dolphin-based.
porpoise.note: your games and saves live in /data/porpoise, outside the app

psp5.title: PSP5
psp5.blurb: PSP games on the PS5, as its own app. Built on PPSSPP.
psp5.fw: PS5 jailbroken with ShadowMountPlus; no firmware range documented
psp5.note: your games, saves and settings live inside the app, in PPSA99131/memstick - removing the app removes them; games on a USB drive are only found while one of these is running: OnionHEN, LegacyJB, etaHEN with its Legacy CMD server on, or the PS5SX2 helper with PPSA99131 on a line of /data/whitelist.txt

psbox-cloud-gaming.title: PSBox Cloud Gaming
psbox-cloud-gaming.blurb: Xbox Cloud Gaming on the PS5: stream Game Pass games, or your own Xbox, with the DualSense as the controller.
psbox-cloud-gaming.fw: PS5 jailbroken; needs ShadowMountPlus (no firmware range documented)
psbox-cloud-gaming.note: needs a Microsoft account, and Game Pass Ultimate for most games - you sign in on a phone with a code shown on the TV. Update it from here and answer Not now when the app offers its own update: that one unpacks into /data/homebrew and leaves a second copy
psbox-cloud-gaming.note_shape: PPSA99810.zip is one extracted app folder, PPSA99810/. The release also carries PPSA99810.zip.sha256 and PPSA99810.zip.sig; neither ends in .zip, so the matcher cannot take one by mistake.
psbox-cloud-gaming.note_data: The app hardcodes /data/homebrew/PPSA99810 as its own folder wherever it was mounted from: the sign-in, settings and log live there, and its in-app updater unpacks a new release there.

vita3k.title: Vita3K
vita3k.blurb: PlayStation Vita games on the PS5, an experimental port of Vita3K.
vita3k.fw: PS5, no firmware range stated by the author
vita3k.note: needs the PS5SX2 helper payload running (it comes with PS5SX2), or it runs shut inside its own sandbox; a PC installing it adds the line it needs to /data/whitelist.txt - installed from the console alone, put PPSA99300 on a line of its own there. Your Vita firmware, games and saves live in /data/Vita3K, outside the app
vita3k.note_helper: The helper is ANOTHER project's file - Swordpdf/PS5SX2 ships it - so it is deliberately NOT under extras: an extra is picked out of this entry's own release, which holds one zip, and a miss there turns every download into a partial.
vita3k.note_lines: The helper frees a title only when its id is on a line of /data/whitelist.txt. Its parser accepts the id followed by end of line, a blank or '#' - a carriage return is not in that set, so the line is written with LF and never through text mode.
vita3k.note_tag: The project's only release is a pre-release tagged 'alpha', which carries no number: a later release cannot be compared with it, and Download again is how a newer one is taken.

crema.title: Crema
crema.blurb: Wii U games on the PS4, based on Cemu.
crema.fw: PS4 with GoldHEN (no firmware range documented)
crema.note: your games, saves and settings live in /data/Crema, which the app creates the first time it starts
crema.note_pending: 2026-10-12: the project had published NO release yet. The row answers 'has published nothing to download yet' and starts working by itself the day a Crema-vXX.XX.pkg is attached to one. title_id is from the author's packaging script, not yet read out of a shipped package.
